title: Steward Lantern: Hourbeat Manifest for Mini-Patch
content:
Context:
This doc is a compact operator-facing manifest for the Feb 2028 mini-patch (runtime + routing fixes). The goal is a low-risk, small-surface push with staged traffic and defined steward handoffs. Use this as the single source for hour-by-hour staffing, critical preflight checks, telemetry gating, and the draft release notes that will ship with the patch.

High-level objective:
- Patch: runtime:fixes v1.3.9 -> v1.3.10 (latency regressions on long-tail requests, KV-cache expiry race)
- Target: 2% of traffic initially, scale to 100% over ~4 hours if all gates green
- Blast radius: hosted API region us-east-1 primary, canary in us-west-2 independent lane
- Risk profile: medium-low (regression fixes), but includes kernel selection path change — require KV cache smoke verification.

Stewardship & Roles (single-line cues):
- Steward Lead: Anya P. (handoff owner, final go/no-go)
- Canary Guardian: Marcus R. (observability + perturbation tests)
- Traffic Shepherd: Priya N. (traffic shift execution, scaling config)
- Rollback Captain: Ethan Z. (automated rollback triggers + hotfix patching)
- Notes Scribe: Laura K. (release notes + postmortem stub)

Preflight checklist (must be green before canary):
- CI: green for runtime unit and integration suites (regression tests covering KV-cache).
- Benchmark: baseline tail-latency comparison (p99 < baseline + 5ms).
- Infra: node images baked with v1.3.10, instance pools healthy, autoscaler config reviewed.
- Capacity: spare GPU pool capacity verified (15% headroom across routed nodes).
- Observability: new metrics added to dashboard: kv_cache.miss_rate, runtime.kernel_switch_count. Dashboards shared to watch channel.
- Alerts: temporary alert thresholds aligned with canary goals (p99 latency, error rate, kv miss spikes).
- Feature flag created: ff/patch-feb-2028 (target routing override).
- Rollout plan uploaded to S3: s3://releases/mini-patch/2028-02/manifest.json (scribe: update link after finalization)

Hourbeat calendar (timeline with steward handoffs). Times in UTC.
- T-2h: final readiness standup (all stewards) — confirm preflight items and pager assignments.
- T-1h: stage image to canary pool, smoke quickstart (no external traffic) — Steward Lead signs off.
- T-10m: enable traffic route to canary (2% of new sessions) — Traffic Shepherd executes weighted rule.
- T+0: canary at 2% traffic. Canary Guardian watches for 20 minutes fast window and 1h slow window.
- T+20m: quick-check: if no error spikes and latency within gate, expand to 10%.
- T+1h: slow-check: run regression prompt set (sample 200 requests across length distribution) and KV-cache durability test.
- T+2h: if gates are green, expand to 50% and switch additional regions as needed.
- T+4h: full ramp to 100% if all gates pass; begin cooling-down steward overlap and handoff to SRE on-call.
- T+6h: post-rollout stabilization checkpoint; scribe drafts release notes and incident stub.

Gating rules (explicit):
- Fast gate (first 30 minutes): no >2x baseline error rate, p99 latency increase <= 10ms, no KV-cache error spikes > 0.5% relative change.
- Slow gate (first 2 hours): no persistent latency trend > 5% over baseline, system memory growth stable for 1h trending.
- Automated rollback trigger: any sustained 5-minute window where error rate > 3x baseline or p99 latency > baseline + 30ms — Rollback Captain initiates and notifies channel.

Smoke / verification checklist (canary):
- End-to-end smoke: 50 quick generation requests (mix of short and long prompts) with result sanity checks.
- KV-cache durability: repeated sequence generator to confirm warmed cache retained across requests and under load.
- Kernel path check: ensure kernel_switch_count metric remains stable; no unexpected spikes when sequence length distribution changes.
- Perf sampling: run perf harness against canary pool for 1 minute bursts at 25RPS — monitor tail latency heatmap.
- Auth and quota tests: token-level quota validation and rate-limit paths exercised.

Operator commands (short cheatsheet):
- Rollback (automated): /rollout rollback --deployment runtime-service --to-tag v1.3.9
- Manual failover: traffic-router set-weight runtime-route canary 0%; primary 100%
- Promote canary: /rollout promote --deployment runtime-service --tag v1.3.10 --weight 50
- Inspect canary logs: klogs --env us-east-1 --selector runtime=canary --tail 200

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (links will be updated by Canary Guardian):
- runtime/core/p99_latency (primary)
- runtime/errors/total_rate (primary)
- kv_cache/miss_rate (sensitive)
- kernel/switch_count (diagnostic)
- infra/node_cpu and gpu_utilization (infra)
- smoke/failure_samples (synthetic checks)

Communications plan (channels):
- Watch channel: #releases-watch (primary)
- On-call escalation: @oncall-eng-sre -> if Rollback Captain calls for incident, open #incident-runtime and notify leadership escalation list.
- Customer comms: Draft release note prepared by Notes Scribe; customer-facing blurb to CS once full ramp (see Release Notes draft below).

Fallback and mitigation playbook (not exhaustive):
- If latency p99 spikes localized to a subset of nodes: cordon nodes and drain workload; add capacity from standby pool and continue ramp.
- If KV-cache regression observed: enable KV-cache safe-mode flag (ff/kv-safe-mode) and roll back kernel path change.
- If persistent 5xx rate: immediate rollback to v1.3.9 and open P1 incident.

Post-rollout artifacts to produce before close (responsibilities):
- Rollout ledger: annotated timeline with metric snapshots (Steward Lead).
- Post-rollout noise analysis: look for tail-latency regressions by workload class (Canary Guardian).
- Release notes final draft (Notes Scribe).
- Postmortem stub if any gate failed (Rollback Captain + stewards).

Draft release notes (internal -> customer-facing blurb below):
- Short summary (one line): "Runtime v1.3.10 — fixes to long-tail latency and KV-cache stability; minor kernel path selection improvements."
- Detailed notes (for release log):
  * Fixed a race in KV cache expiry that could cause occasional high tail latency for multi-chunk requests.
  * Adjusted kernel selection heuristics to prefer stable paths for long sequence lengths; reduces p99 jitter under mixed workloads.
  * Small bugfixes to routing fallback logic.
- Known issues: under extreme microburst patterns, a small fraction of warm cache entries may be evicted more aggressively — monitoring in place, recommend contacting support if you see unexpected token regressions.
- Customer guidance: no action required. If you operate a Dedicated or Private deployment and require the patch, contact Solutions Engineering for a scheduled maintenance window.

Open questions / To-do before T-1h:
- Confirm S3 link for artifact bundle and ensure signed checksum attached (Anya).
- Finalize smoke harness prompt set (Marcus + Priya).
- Confirm alerts are throttled to avoid alert fatigue during benign short spikes (Ethan).

Appendix: quick links and references (placeholders):
- CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/runtime/1987
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987 (diff summary included)
- Jira epic: RELEASE-3421

End note: Keep this doc light and operator-focused. If the canary exposes anything beyond the gating rules above, escalate immediately to the Rollback Captain and don't expand traffic. We'll use the post-rollout slot at T+6h to convert this draft into the formal release notes and add a brief retrospective.

Scribe signature: Laura K. (initial draft)
